# Slice 3 closed: five things the review must see, one of them a false reason shipped in slice 1

Records 17 (RED) and 18 (GREEN) close slice 3. Verified independently of the report: record 17
exits 1 on `argparse: invalid choice: 'hook'`, and the substitution is stated inside the
recorded output rather than claimed afterwards. `doctor` is clean across fourteen sections
after `sync`, and both copies carry the graphify entries, the repowise entries and the
permissions block untouched beside the harness's.

## 1. The `clients` reason in harness/hooks.json is now known to be false

Slice 1 gave PreCompact and SubagentStop to Claude Code alone and wrote the reason into the
source: "Codex documents no compaction hook" and "Codex has no subagent-stop event". Slice 3
disproved both from the tool itself. The codex-cli 0.156.1 binary carries a JSON Schema per
hook event, and `strings` on it prints twenty-three of them, titled `pre-tool-use.command.input`,
`session-start.command.output` and so on; they show Codex supporting PreCompact and
SubagentStop, and PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, SubagentStart, PostCompact, SessionEnd and
Interrupt besides.

So the withholding is a decision with a reason that is not true, which is worse than either
behaviour would be. It is left standing rather than fixed in this session for one reason: the
fix is a one-line `clients` change that adds two Codex entries no fixture covers and no
criterion asks for, and choosing between correcting the reason and correcting the behaviour is
the review's to make, not a thing to slip in over budget. The evidence is here so it is made
with the schema in hand.

## 2. harness/guard.py changed outside slice 3's file list, and it was a real defect

The PreToolUse payload carries `tool_input.file_path` as an absolute path, and `_relative`
compared it literally against the root. Where a parent is a symlink, which is `/var` on macOS
and so every temporary project the suite builds, the two strings differ: the path read as
outside the project, matched no slice file, and every edit of that session was refused. It now
tries the literal comparison and then both sides resolved, and slice 2's `test_guard.py` was
re-run inside record 18.

The fix belongs in `decide` rather than in the hook, because `harness guard /abs/path` typed by
a person has the same defect. It is the second file this ticket has touched outside a slice's
list, after `harness/tests/helpers.py` in record 13, and for the same kind of reason: the list
was drawn before the defect was known.

## 3. The guard does not see a write through a shell, and this session is the proof

The PreToolUse matcher is `Edit|Write|MultiEdit|apply_patch`, so an edit made by a shell
heredoc or `sed` is never judged. Slice 3's own edits went through Bash for that reason, which
means the live guard judged none of them and there is no refusal to report from building it.
The skill now says which hole the hooks leave rather than claiming this ticket closes it. Worth
stating plainly because criterion 2 is proven by fixtures, and a reader could otherwise take
fixtures passing as the wall standing.

## 4. kpi.py reads every handoff record as a slice boundary

A pack written by PreCompact in the middle of a slice therefore closes a token window early and
the sprint report's tokens-per-slice figure is low by that much. The record carries `auto: true`
so a reader can tell the two apart, and `kpi.py` is unchanged because it was in no slice's list.
The figure is wrong in a knowable direction rather than silently.

## 5. Claude Code's SubagentStop payload key for the agent name is unverified

`_agent_that_stopped` accepts `agent_type`, `subagent_type` and `agent_name` and stays silent
when none is present, so on the Claude Code side that hook may do nothing until a live session
settles which key arrives. The Codex side is verified from the schemas; this side is not.

## What is left before this ticket can advance out of review

Criterion 5 is unmet and cannot be met from here: it asks what an interactive Codex session
prints for `/hooks` and whether a guarded edit is refused there, and whether `.agents/settings.json`
is read by anything. Everything the schemas can settle is settled; the session itself is not.
That is Ruud's, and the ticket does not leave review without the note.
